The SJC denied the complaint 18-4-0, finding the JC's dismissal of Indictment 1 under BCO 32-20 (passage of time) was within its…

artifacts.title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained the Session of FPC North Port's complaint that Southwest Florida Presbytery erred when it remanded a previously out-of-order complaint back to the Session and when it directed and instructed the Session to initiate formal ecclesiastical process against a member without following the required steps of BCO 40-5. The Commission held that once the Original CM Complaint was found out of order, there was no matter for Presbytery to carry forward, and any subsequent instructions to the Session to initiate process were null and void.

artifacts.title: Brown v. Northern California Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church complained that Louisiana Presbytery improperly assumed original jurisdiction over church member Mike Holland, barring him from the Lord's Table for contumacy after he was cited in SPLC reporting regarding Auburn Avenue Presbyterian Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that because Delhi Session had investigated and acted under BCO 31-2, Louisiana Presbytery lacked grounds to assume original jurisdiction under BCO 33-1, rendering its judgment against Holland a nullity; three dissenting opinions argued the SJC lacked appellate review of the jurisdiction question because no timely complaint was filed against the assumption of jurisdiction itself.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Charles Kim appealed discipline imposed by a Korean Capital Presbytery commission that had replaced the Session of the Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington. The SJC held that original jurisdiction over a communicant member belonged to the Session, not the presbytery commission, reversed the presbytery's action and censure, and held that the commission's acts were unauthorized without congregational consent.

artifacts.title: Appeal Deacon Samuel Hong v. Korean Capital Presbytery 30-30, III, p. 142
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission reversed the Korean Capital Presbytery's censure of Deacon Samuel Hong, finding that the Presbytery lacked original jurisdiction over communicant members and should have been tried in the Session. The court held that regardless of the merits of the underlying charges (contumacy and making false statements), the procedural violation of jurisdiction was fatal to the action.

artifacts.title: Appeal RE Choon Soon Lee v. Korean Capital Presbytery 30-30, III, p. 149
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission reversed the Korean Capital Presbytery's action in adjudicating charges against RE Choon Soon Lee. The court held that a ruling elder member of a local congregation may only be subject to judicial process originating in the Session of that church, not in the Presbytery, as the Session has original jurisdiction over its members.

artifacts.title: Appeal RE Joo Bok Suh v. Korean Capital Presbytery 30-30, III, p. 147
artifacts.synopsis: Appeal by RE Joo Bok Suh challenging the Korean Capital Presbytery's attempt to exercise original jurisdiction over charges of making false statements on official documents related to church trustee replacement. The Standing Judicial Commission reversed the presbytery's action, holding that original jurisdiction over communicant members must reside with the Session of the church to which they belong, not with the Presbytery.

The SJC sustained the complaint, held that the presbytery lacked authority to take that action under the BCO and Preliminary Principle Six, and annulled the commission's subsequent acts.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace Reformed Presbyterian Church appealed its conviction for contumacy and termination of its relationship with Heartland Presbytery. The SJC reversed the conviction, holding that a presbytery lacks original jurisdiction to indict and try a session (lower court) for an offense such as contumacy, as BCO provisions reserve original jurisdiction over ruling elders to the Session level.

artifacts.synopsis: Bruce Nickoley and David Stephens complained against Southwest Presbytery's actions in withdrawing charges against two ruling elders, dissolving a pastoral relationship, and rescinding its suspension of a local church session. The SJC denied the complaint, affirming that the Presbytery correctly determined it lacked constitutional authority to suspend the session or act as a 'Session pro tem' without congregational consent, and that original jurisdiction over charges against ruling elders rested with the local session.

artifacts.title: Bowen v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE David Bowen complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's actions rescinding its 1988 decision and annulling the elections and ordinations of ruling elders and deacons at the Church of the Good Shepherd who took exception to infant baptism and limited atonement. The SJC sustained the complaint that ECP erred in rescinding a two-year-old action and annulling ordinations without due process under BCO 24-6, while also affirming that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals of the system of doctrine for which no exceptions may be granted for church officers.
